metadata.title: A tool to capture learning experiences during COVID-19 (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document describes the development of the PISA Global Crises Module instruments (student and school questionnaire items) rather than reporting an analysis of PISA microdata with statistical estimation. As such, it does not specify whether complex survey weights or replicate weights were applied to produce estimates. For any future implementation using PISA microdata, analysts should use the official PISA sampling/survey weights provided in the international database for the relevant cycle and follow the standard replicate-weight procedure (if available) to obtain correct uncertainty under the complex design. Because the module is intended for adaptation and broader implementation, weighting guidance should be aligned with the host PISA cycle’s technical documentation and the specific countries’ implementation decisions.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework/instrument-development report that does not present an empirical model predicting cognitive outcomes with plausible values (PVs). The module focuses on questionnaire constructs (e.g., awareness, school closure experiences, digital device use, learning impressions) rather than reporting PV-based achievement scores, so PV handling is not applicable. Missing-data handling is not reported because no estimation model or dataset analysis is conducted in the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report describes instrument development for the PISA Global Crises Module, including small-scale cognitive interview studies in three countries, but it does not provide an analytic student sample or specify inclusion/exclusion criteria for a quantitative dataset.

data.outcome_summary: The OECD report introduces the PISA Global Crises Module as a tool to capture students’ learning experiences, school closure context, and related well-being during COVID-19 disruptions. It specifies that the module contains 62 student questionnaire items (grouped into 11 constructs) and 68 school questionnaire items (grouped into 14 constructs), developed through expert input, PISA National Centres, and small-scale cognitive interviews in three countries. The module is designed to help policymakers and researchers examine differential effects on learning and well-being and to document the degree and nature of educational interruption across education systems. The document does not report any student-level predictive modeling, scaling, plausible values, or performance metrics; instead, it provides the instruments and construct descriptions to support adaptation and implementation. Consequently, no benchmarks or effect sizes are reported in the provided text.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the provided text is limited to the abstract and high-level section headings, and the document is primarily an instrument-development/technical tool description rather than an empirical ML study. Therefore, there is no reported analytic sample size, country-level breakdown, weighting scheme, missing-data strategy, or model performance to extract. The module’s constructs are enumerated (e.g., ST197, ST347–ST356; SC158, SC213–SC224), but the report does not present predictive outcomes, so main findings and ML technique fields are intentionally left empty.
